brief: Goldman's Lee flows note: Friday saw unprecedented index-protection buying (VIX futures at 3.6x average volume, record Cboe put volume) following weeks of damage to individual stocks, resembling the volume pattern before August 2024's VIX spike above 60. A quality pair trade (GSP1QUAL) hit a 12-month high as rising rates hit long-duration, levered, unprofitable names, consistent with HY underperforming IG. Tighter financial conditions are driving rotation into defensives over cyclicals. Prime data shows managers cutting gross and net leverage and L/S ratios to multi-year lows while still holding long books, leaving room for further de-grossing if pressure continues, and global equities were net sold broadly. The AI winners-vs-at-risk pair trade is flat on the year after being up near 100% through June, as AI and hyperscaler credit spreads hit yearly wides and hedge funds reversed all 2025 net AI buying over five sessions. Info Tech was the most net-sold sector even as leveraged ETFs (SOXL, TQQQ) saw record inflows. Goldman's Ben Snider expects slowing but still solid 2027 growth and cautions against Momentum exposure given narrow breadth, favoring consumer laggards and defensive-quality names. Bottom-up, Goldman raises its server TAM and flags a lasting memory technology gap versus CXMT.
